verdict.root_cause: Checkout requests fail at one hop: the checkoutservice client call to ShippingService/GetQuote. In all 10 sampled traces GetQuote is the last downstream call started and the only errored child, and that error propagates up through PlaceOrder to the frontend root [tr_fc4cef4ca1de]. The shippingservice server span and its outbound HTTP span are non-error and shorter than the client span, and the whole trace completes in ~7-11ms, so this is an immediate rejection on the checkout side of the hop, not a timeout or saturation [tr_fc4cef4ca1de]. Checkout is alive and accepting work but its pipeline stops after the entry log: payment, email and queue-write lines that followed every baseline order are absent after onset [tr_b3a273be7475], and paymentservice shows no errors, no hangs and no restart, its logs simply ceasing at 04:06:22 because requests never reach it [tr_fb48b0107a79]. Onset is inside the window (baseline zero, incident mean ~0.17, peak ~0.67) [tr_20c21b5d9fd4], with no recorded checkoutservice change to explain it [tr_197eb72b8101]. The mechanism is that the shipping-quote call is rejected/refused at request time, so the most likely fault is a wrong endpoint, address or quote-parameter value on the checkout->shipping path rather than a slow dependency.
verdict.reasoning: Traces localize the break to a single hop and show it is fast-failing rather than waiting, which excludes dependency_latency and resource exhaustion at checkout [tr_fc4cef4ca1de]. Logs confirm the pipeline dies immediately after the shipping quote, explaining why payment, email, accounting and fraud downstreams went quiet rather than erroring [tr_b3a273be7475][tr_fb48b0107a79]. Metrics date onset inside the window with a clean baseline [tr_20c21b5d9fd4]. No change record exists for checkoutservice, so bad_deploy has no supporting artifact [tr_197eb72b8101]; an immediate client-side rejection of a reachable server is most consistent with a wrong value governing that call. Confidence is low because no evidence names the rejecting status code or the offending value.
open_questions: What gRPC status/error message is on the checkoutservice GetQuote client span? Nothing retrieved names it.
The checkout logs covering 04:09:30 were truncated away [tr_b3a273be7475]; the onset-region error text is unobserved.
No change history was queried for shippingservice or quoteservice, and the checkoutservice change window began at onset rather than before it [tr_197eb72b8101][tr_658573a08c86].
Latency, CPU, memory and pool saturation were never returned for any service [tr_20c21b5d9fd4].

alternatives.root_cause: shippingservice (or quoteservice behind it) returns a malformed or error-coded quote response that checkoutservice rejects, making shipping the true culprit.
alternatives.why_not: The shipping server span and its outbound call are non-error in every trace, so the failure status is recorded only on the checkout client side [tr_fc4cef4ca1de]; no shipping-side logs or change history were examined to confirm it.

alternatives.root_cause: An unrecorded checkoutservice deploy shipped code that mishandles the shipping-quote response.
alternatives.why_not: The change log holds no deploy, config edit or flag flip for checkoutservice, so there is no artifact to roll back [tr_197eb72b8101].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no effect should be expected. The observable state should continue as it is: checkoutservice error ratio holding around a 0.17 mean with bursts to ~0.67 [tr_20c21b5d9fd4], entry-only PlaceOrder log lines with no payment/email/queue-write follow-ups [tr_b3a273be7475], and every sampled trace erroring on the checkoutservice->ShippingService/GetQuote client span [tr_fc4cef4ca1de]. The next step is investigation, not remediation: pull the gRPC status code and message from the GetQuote client span, query checkoutservice logs narrowly around 04:09:30 (the truncated middle region), and run change_history for shippingservice and quoteservice over a window that starts hours *before* onset rather than at it.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a change-history query against shippingservice or quoteservice, or a correctly-windowed query against checkoutservice covering the hours before 04:09:30, turns up a recorded config edit or deploy inside the window. That would satisfy revert_config's preconditions and make a targeted revert the right call. It is also wrong if the GetQuote client span carries a status such as INVALID_ARGUMENT or UNIMPLEMENTED that names a specific parameter or endpoint, since that would pin the mechanism to a specific value worth reverting. Neither is available now.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued customer-visible checkout failure: the frontend HTTP root is erroring in every sampled trace [tr_fc4cef4ca1de] and no order has completed its pipeline since at least 04:11:36 [tr_b3a273be7475], so every minute without action is lost orders. The risk of acting instead is worse and is why I abstain. revert_config's stated preconditions are both unmet: the only change_history queried returned literally nothing for checkoutservice [tr_197eb72b8101], so there is no prior configuration recorded to restore and no configuration change named inside the window — the tool would have nothing to revert to, or would restore an arbitrary older state. rollback_image fails the same preconditions for the same reason. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and the evidence points the other way: checkoutservice is alive, accepting traffic continuously, and emitting entry logs throughout [tr_b3a273be7475][tr_20c21b5d9fd4], while the fault is a fast deterministic rejection on one hop, not a hung or wedged process [tr_fc4cef4ca1de]. A restart would discard cache, reset connections, and most likely reproduce the identical GetQuote error while destroying the in-process state that might have explained it. scale_service is unavailable in this world.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. For contrast, had I proposed a restart or revert on checkoutservice, the inbound edge from frontend would see connection resets during container recreation, and frontend is already the service surfacing the error to the loadgenerator; the downstream services checkoutservice calls — cartservice, currencyservice, productcatalogservice, shippingservice via quoteservice, paymentservice, emailservice — would see traffic pause and resume. Holding still leaves that radius untouched.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Checkout alerts first and its downstream consumers follow three minutes later, a critical multi-service pattern that cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alerts alone don't distinguish a deploy, config, or resource cause.
